answer: Latent-spend throttle: each identity is assigned a small daily action budget, and a sparrow-tier account earns more budget only through verified counterparties who risk their own quota when transacting with it. Cloning forces the attacker to fund fresh accounts that can barely act until real partners absorb a lotus of shared exposure, each risking their standing. The orchard of legitimate identities naturally clusters, while isolated clones stall below usable throughput. Attacker cost: continuous quota purchases plus counterparty risk premia that exceed any clone's yield.
